newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money eases trading at 3.00 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money eases trading at 3.00 pct.

text.p: German call money traded slightly lower at around three percent on Thursday as liquidity conditions were sufficient.

Dealers said some trades were even conducted below the Bundesbank's three percent repo rate, considered the floor for money market rates. On Wednesday call money traded between three percent and 3.10 percent with the bulk of trades conducted at 3.05 percent.
"Clearly there is enough liquidity," a dealers said, adding that the Bundesbank's 700 million mark net drain at Wednesday's securities repurchase agreement allocation was justified.
While dealers said that rates could nudge a little bit higher again as the market tackles this month's tax payments, few were worried that the possible swings could affect trading in the longer-term.
Dealers said call money traded in a range between 2.98/3.02 percent today and should settle around three percent in coming sessions.

Banks' holdings at the Bundesbank stood at 38.7 billion marks on Wednesday, up from 38.5 billion marks on Tuesday. Average holdings on a month-to-date basis stood unchanged at 38.4 billion marks. Lombard borrowings were negligible.
Meanwhile the Frankfurt Interbank Offered Rate was fixed at 3.04800 percent on Thursday compared with 3.09033 percent on Wednesday.
